title: Trump, Xi and Putin to hold first three-way meeting at APEC
h1: Trump, Xi and Putin plan their first three-way meeting this week on the sidelines of the APEC summit in Shenzhen
description: The White House and the Kremlin confirmed on November 13 and 14, 2026 that Trump, Xi and Putin will meet Thursday at APEC in Shenzhen to talk about nuclear arms.
standfirst: The leaders of the three biggest nuclear powers have never met together. U.S. officials say the talks will center on nuclear weapons and that no agreement is expected.
keywords: Trump Xi Putin meeting, APEC Shenzhen 2026, trilateral summit, New START expired, nuclear arms talks China, Trump China trip, Peskov Yalta
takeaways: The meeting is planned for Thursday, November 19, on the sidelines of the APEC summit in Shenzhen, China, the Associated Press reported.
The White House confirmed the plan on Friday, November 13, and the Kremlin confirmed it on Saturday, November 14.
A senior U.S. official said no agreements are expected; the last U.S.-Russia nuclear arms treaty, New START, expired in February.
body: President Donald Trump, Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin plan to meet together for the first time this week. The three-way meeting is set for Thursday on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in Shenzhen, China, the Associated Press reported. The White House confirmed the plan on Friday, and the Kremlin did so on Saturday.

Nuclear weapons, mainly. The New START treaty between Washington and Moscow lapsed in February, which left the two largest arsenals without limits for the first time in more than 50 years. Trump turned down a Russian offer to extend it for a year and has called for a new deal that includes China.
The sizes are uneven. The Pentagon estimates that China has more than 600 warheads, while the United States and Russia are each estimated to hold more than 5,000, according to the AP.
Trump also plans to raise the Iran war with Xi and Putin but will steer clear of Russia's war in Ukraine, a senior U.S. official said, Al Jazeera reported.

U.S. officials are playing down expectations. "We do not expect to get to any kind of agreement," a senior Trump administration official told Reuters, according to Al Jazeera. The official described the session as the start of a conversation. Analysts told the AP the meeting is likely to be more symbolic than substantive.

Some commentators have compared the gathering to the 1945 Yalta Conference, where the leaders of the United States, Britain and the Soviet Union shaped the order that followed World War II. Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov rejected the comparison and said nothing agreed in Shenzhen can be imposed on others, though he called the meeting "extremely significant."

The APEC summit brings 21 economies to Shenzhen. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has said he is worried the three leaders could use the meeting to discuss a deal on Ukraine without Kyiv at the table. Trump is not expected to meet North Korean leader Kim Jong Un during the Asia trip, Al Jazeera reported.
